user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN → Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Migration (Night Before)
- [ ] Install `git-svn` or `svn2git`
- [ ] Audit SVN repo size and history depth
- [ ] Create author mapping file (`authors.txt`)

```
jsmith = John Smith <jsmith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mjones@company.com>
```

---

## Morning (2–3 hrs): Convert

### 1. Clone SVN repo
```bash
git svn clone https://svn.example.com/repo \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  --stdlayout \
  -s \
  my-repo
```

### 2. Clean up SVN artifacts
```bash
cd my-repo

# Convert SVN tags to Git tags
git for-each-ref refs/remotes/tags | cut -d / -f 5- | while read tag; do
  git tag "$tag" "refs/remotes/tags/$tag"
  git branch -r -d "tags/$tag"
done

# Convert SVN branches to Git branches
git for-each-ref refs/remotes | grep -v tags | cut -d / -f 4- | while read branch; do
  git branch "$branch" "refs/remotes/$branch"
  git branch -r -d "$branch"
done
```

### 3. Verify history
```bash
git log --oneline | head -20
git branch -a
git tag
```

---

## Midday (1–2 hrs): Validate

- [ ] Compare file counts: SVN checkout vs Git working tree
- [ ] Spot-check 5–10 commits for accuracy
- [ ] Confirm all branches/tags present
- [ ] Run build/tests on migrated repo

```bash
# Quick file count check
svn export https://svn.example.com/repo/trunk svn-export
diff -rq svn-export my-repo --exclude=".git"
```

---

## Afternoon (1–2 hrs): Push & Configure

### 1. Push to remote (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket)
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/org/my-repo.git
git push origin --all
git push origin --tags
```

### 2. Set up branch protections
- Protect `main`/`master`
- Require PR reviews

### 3. Update CI/CD pipelines
- Point to new Git remote URL
- Update any SVN-specific commands

---

## End of Day: Cutover

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 🔒 | **Lock SVN repo** (set to read-only) |
| 📢 | Notify team of new Git URL |
| 📄 | Update README/wiki with Git workflow |
| 🗑️ | Schedule SVN decommission (30 days) |

---

## Rollback Plan
> Keep SVN read-only (don't delete) for 30 days in case issues arise.

---

## Tools
| Tool | Use Case |
|------|----------|
| `git svn` | Built-in, good for standard layouts |
| `svn2git` | Cleaner CLI wrapper |
| `reposurgeon` | Complex histories |

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🗺️ Incomplete Author Mapping
**Risk:** Commits with unmapped authors fail or show as `unknown`
**Mitigation:** Run `svn log | grep "^r" | awk '{print $3}' | sort -u` to extract **all** authors before migrating — not just recent ones.

---

### 2. 🌿 Mangled Branches/Tags
**Risk:** Non-standard SVN layouts (e.g., nested branches, multiple trunk copies) convert incorrectly or are silently skipped
**Mitigation:** Audit with `svn ls ^/branches` beforehand; verify branch/tag count matches post-migration.

---

### 3. ⏱️ History Rewrite Surprises
**Risk:** Binary files or large commits bloat the Git repo; `--no-metadata` strips SVN revision refs that teams rely on (`r1234`)
**Mitigation:** Run `git count-objects -vH` post-migration; consider `git-filter-repo` to strip large blobs, and decide **upfront** whether to keep SVN metadata.

---

> **Biggest single risk:** Cutting over before validating CI/CD — leaves the team unable to ship.

## Migration Checklist

### Before
- [ ] Back up SVN repo
- [ ] Extract all authors, build `authors.txt`
- [ ] Audit branches/tags layout

### During
- [ ] Run conversion with author mapping
- [ ] Verify branch and tag count
- [ ] Diff file tree vs SVN trunk
- [ ] Run build/tests

### After
- [ ] Push to remote
- [ ] Lock SVN to read-only
- [ ] Notify team
- [ ] Update CI/CD pipelines
Keep SVN **read-only but accessible** for 30 days — if issues arise, revert CI/CD pipelines to the original SVN URL and resume work there.
Install `git-svn` on the machine performing the migration.
